subject.title: [Feature] Pre-response enforcement hooks (hard gates) for mandatory tool-call / policy rules

question: Should OpenClaw add a versioned fail-closed final-response gate to core/plugin APIs, and what default, retry, audit, and operator-control semantics should it have?
rationale: This cannot be safely resolved as a narrow repair because it changes final response delivery, plugin API contracts, fail-closed security behavior, and compatibility expectations for existing agents and plugins.

options.title: Design a versioned response-gate API
options.body: Add the core lifecycle seam and keep domain-specific validators/policy packs in plugins, with explicit defaults, audit records, retry caps, and upgrade guidance before implementation.

options.title: Scope to existing hooks and plugin docs
options.body: Document current before_tool_call, before_agent_finalize, and message hooks as the supported policy surface, accepting that they do not provide this issue's hard pre-response guarantee.

options.title: Split into narrower security issues first
options.body: Create separate maintainer-owned design tracks for mandatory tool ledgers, public-action approval envelopes, and outbound pre-send gates before any shared responseGate API is attempted.

recommendation.title: Design a versioned response-gate API
recommendation.body: Add the core lifecycle seam and keep domain-specific validators/policy packs in plugins, with explicit defaults, audit records, retry caps, and upgrade guidance before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history for the closest hook/API seam is the before_agent_finalize implementation and related harness hook work.
